name: portals to the Otherworld

attributes.attribute: parallel time and place near to this world
approachable through dolmens, stone circles, and hillforts
veil thinned at Beltane and Samhain

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Celtic Otherworld is a cosmological concept. It is not a place apart from this world. There is no heaven high above or hell far below. The Otherworld exists in a parallel time and place. It sits close to this world yet stays out of reach. Certain sites and times offered portals to it. Dolmens, stone circles, and hillforts served as such portals. The veil between the worlds thinned at these places. The chief crossing times fell on Beltane, May 1, and on Samhain, November 1. Then beings could slip from one world to the next.

okr.objective: Explain the Otherworld as a parallel realm reached through symbolic portals.
key_results: States the Otherworld as a parallel time and place, not a distant heaven or hell
Names dolmens, stone circles, and hillforts as entry points
Names Beltane and Samhain as the chief crossing times
